description.narrative: Our initiative is a women-centered highland agricultural and livelihood empowerment program implemented in Muong Khuong district and Pha Long district, focusing on the indigenous mandarin value chain. The project aims to enhance sustainable livelihoods and elevate the social status of ethnic minority women by supporting equitable access to science and technology in cultivation, post-harvest processing, product innovation, and market-oriented commercialization. At the same time, it strengthens climate resilience and reduces gender inequality in agricultural economic participation and leadership. The initiative has three core objectives: (1) build farmers’ technical capacity-especially women-in climate-adaptive, bio-safe, and market-oriented mandarin production; (2) support women-led collective economic institutions to sustainably govern and operate key nodes in the value chain; and (3) co-design gender-responsive, evidence-based rural development policy engagement. Key activities include structured technical training on soil-smart fertilization, climate-adaptive orchard design, IPM-aligned pest and disease management, safe post-harvest technologies, small-scale processing, product diversification (e.g., dehydrated snacks, essential oils, mandarin-infused beverages), packaging, quality assurance, traceability, and digital marketing. Business incubation support helps establish women-led cooperative economies, foster peer learning networks, improve value chain coordination, and develop sustainable market linkages and local branding that protect indigenous identity while enabling fair benefit sharing. The initiative targets four main indicators: (1) 360 training attendances with at least 70%ethnic minority women; (2) 2 women-led cooperative groups operating sustainably as value-chain focal actors; (3) 2 cultivation pilot models integrating scientific techniques with indigenous practices for climate resilience; and (4) 2 participatory policy proposals co-formulated with local authorities, social organizations, and community voices to promote inclusive, gender-responsive agricultural economic development. The project is implemented over two years, directly benefiting ethnic minority women farmers, their households, and local agricultural networks, creating long-term gains in income, status, leadership, and climate-resilient production systems.

participating-org.narrative: The Institute of Scientific Research and Application (ISRA) of Hanoi Pedagogical University 2 was established in 2016, evolving from the former Center for Scientific Research Support and Technology Transfer. As a key unit promoting research, innovation, and technology application within the university, ISRA plays an essential role in supporting training quality, scientific development, and community engagement. The Institute is equipped with a strong research infrastructure, including 12 specialized laboratories and one pilot-scale production room, enabling research in chemistry, biology, biotechnology, and materials science. Its professional team includes six full-time staff members with diverse expertise, ranging from senior lecturers and principal specialists to researchers andlaboratory technicians. ISRA has implemented several major equipment projects and actively collaborates with local organizations and enterprises, such as the Vinh Phuc Center for Scientific and Technological Advancement, the Lai Chau Center for Science and Technology Assessment and Development, and private sector partners in Hanoi. These partnerships enhance the Institute’s capacity for applied research and technology transfer. For the period 2020–2025, ISRA aims to become adynamic and innovative research and technology development center within the university system. By 2030, the Institute envisions becoming a leading linkage model connecting the university with regional science and technology organizations, particularly in the Midlands and Northern Mountainous region.
